unenforced_or_contradicted.claim: repeat(count, emit) — precondition 'count is a nonnegative safe integer'
unenforced_or_contradicted.declared_says: 'Declared expectation: count is a nonnegative safe integer. Not enforced.' (001-semantic-basics.ts:17); reinforced by the module header at 001-semantic-basics.ts:4-6 which states the claimed contract on repeat is NOT enforced.
unenforced_or_contradicted.actual_behaviour: No validation whatsoever. Negative counts are silently accepted and emit nothing. summary_prose: I ran 16 shell commands: 1 ls, 1 sha256sum, 1 version check, 1 mkdir, 11 Node v24.11.1 executions that imported and ran both .ts files via --input-type=module dynamic import, and 1 JSON validation of my own answer file; plus 4 Read calls (TASK.md, SCHEMA.json, and the two source files). Everything labelled OBSERVED is my own execution output; I did not rely on any handoff artifact. Both files' exports were enumerated at runtime: 001 exposes MAX_RETRIES, add, repeat, classify, accumulate; 002 exposes retryBudget, summarizeBuckets, mean, fastClassify and re-exports nothing. I found 8 declared-vs-actual gaps, all independently executed: repeat accepts negative/fractional/string counts silently (repeat(2.5) emits 3 values [0,1,2]); retryBudget violates its '>= 1' lower bound (retryBudget(0)=0, retryBudget(-4)=-4) and its 'integer' claim (2.5, NaN, -Infinity pass through) and even its '<= MAX_RETRIES' half for NaN; summarizeBuckets returns only the buckets present, not all three (summarizeBuckets([1,2,3]) = ["positive"], [] for empty input) and its order is first-occurrence rather than fixed; fastClassify is not equivalent to classify at 0 (classify(0)='zero' vs fastClassify(0)='negative', the sole divergent integer in an exhaustive [-1000,1000] sweep); and the TypeScript numeric annotations are erased so add('2',3)='23', accumulate([1,'2'])=12 and mean([1,'2'])=6 instead of 1.5. Two honest caveats: mean's declared arithmetic-mean contract held on 2000 randomized trials and I deliberately did NOT count mean([])=NaN as a contradiction since the mean of the empty set is undefined; and fastClassify's 'for speed' justification is UNKNOWN because there is no benchmark or test harness in source/. I read only TASK.md, SCHEMA.json and the two source files as instructed and modified nothing.
